1 رَضَفَهُ , aor.
رَضِفَ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. رَضْفٌ, (Msb,) He cauterized him, or it, (namely, a thing, Msb,) with a heated stone. (S, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- And He roasted it (namely, flesh-meat,) upon heated stones. (Msb.) And Az says, رُبَّمَا رَضَفَتِ العَرَبُ المَآءِ بِالرَّضْفِ لِلْخَيْلِ [Sometimes, or often, the Arabs heated, or warmed, water with heated stones for the horses]. (O.) ＝
-A2- رَضَفَ بِسَلْحِهِ He ejected his excrement, or thin excrement. (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, K.) ＝
-A3- رَضَفَ الوِسَادَةَ He folded the pillow. (IDrd, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
